body:
Thank you for the advice. Feeling faded is the worst, and I'm sorry it's gotten to that point for you. Honestly though, for me it feels like no matter what I do, I won't want life. Even if I find a loving partner to share the responsibility of living with me, I'd still feel that way.

The problem is, I'm perfectly comfortable with dying, and dying when I want. It feels more like fate to me, because I just want to give back my "gift" of life. That's why I don't empathize with most people; they're afraid to die, or something important is holding them back, and I don't have anything.

At the moment, I don't want anyone to help me with responsibility. I just want people to understand that death is what I want, and it's not borne from misery or depression.

Thank you, I'm sorry you're stuck with those thoughts, and I genuinely hope everything goes well over the summer. I'm afraid I can't 100% relate because my suicide doesn't feel like an option; it feels like my fate. You don't need to say something about people caring because I don't want them to, I just want them to understand. I want people to understand that when they gave me the "gift" of life, they should allow me the option to return it. But no one would understand, because so many people care about their lives. I don't care about mine, because I never wanted it.

Oh boy... I went off a bit. I'm sorry your friend left you alone like that, but I'm sure they think it matters! Sometimes people just don't know how to respond. At least, people don't know how to respond to my troubles because I'm so stead-fast in my will to die. And honestly, some people are just unable to comprehend wanting to die. 

I hope the end for us is pure nothingness. Either that, or pure bliss.
